findings.summary: A book point is missing from these pages.
findings.evidence: useMemo around a trivial expression (`useMemo(() => a + b, [a,b])`) — the hook costs more than the addition.
findings.fix: Add this point to a page — the fit pass may only add, so it is safe to run.

findings.summary: The React Compiler callout presents automatic memoization as React 19 version behaviour, when the compiler is a separate opt-in build-time tool that is not enabled by installing React 19 and is not restricted to React 19.
findings.evidence: "React Compiler" / "React 19+ auto-inserts memoization, so most hand-written memo/useMemo/useCallback is unnecessary in compiled code."
findings.fix: Reword to: "React Compiler (stable 1.0, Oct 2025) is an opt-in build step — install babel-plugin-react-compiler; React 19 alone does not memoize anything. It also supports React 17/18 via react-compiler-runtime. Where it applies, most hand-written memo/useMemo/useCallback becomes unnecessary."

findings.summary: useDeferredValue and startTransition are recommended in a fix table and again in the closing decision flow, but the handbook never says what they do.
findings.evidence: Page 8 §31 table: ["heavy list while typing","useDeferredValue"], ["slow non-urgent update","startTransition"] — and page 10 §44: "Huge lists: virtualize. Heavy updates: useDeferredValue." No bullet anywhere states the mechanism (the syllabus line "mark an update as non-urgent, keeping typing responsive while a heavy list re-renders in the background" is absent).
findings.fix: Add one bullet under §31: "Both mark an update as non-urgent — React keeps typing responsive and re-renders the heavy list in the background." so the two names in the final checklist are actionable.

findings.summary: "Reconciliation" — the concept named in the series title — is used for the first time in the page-10 recap; the chapter that teaches it never uses the word.
findings.evidence: Page 10 §42: "Reconciliation matches by (type, position), then key." The teaching sections are titled "7. The Diffing Goal" and "8. Match or Destroy" and speak only of "diffing"; the word reconciliation appears nowhere before the summary.
findings.fix: Retitle page 2 §7 to "Reconciliation: The Diffing Goal" and open its first bullet with "Reconciliation = old tree + new tree → minimal set of DOM operations," so the recap refers back to a named idea.

findings.summary: The element-shape comment lists `ref` as a top-level field of the React element, but React 19 moved ref into props and removed element.ref.
findings.evidence: "const el = <Row id={1} />;  // jsx() call" / "// { type: Row, props:{id:1}, key, ref }"
findings.fix: Change the comment to `// { type: Row, props:{ id:1, ref }, key }` (React 19: ref is a regular prop; element.ref was removed).

findings.summary: Page 1 asserts React computes the minimal DOM delta, which overstates the heuristic diff and contradicts the handbook's own index-key example.
findings.evidence: "UI = f(state); React computes the minimal DOM delta." vs. page 2 sidebox "Every row gets patched instead of one insert."
findings.fix: Replace with "React computes a small DOM delta with an O(n) heuristic diff — near-minimal, not provably minimal" so it agrees with §7's "The Diffing Goal" framing.

findings.summary: A key change is taught as a trigger before the key prop has been introduced.
findings.evidence: Page 2 §5: "forceUpdate, or a key change on the element." / "A key change is a remount, not a re-render." The key prop is first mentioned two sections later (§7: "Heuristic 2: you hint stable identity with the key prop") and only defined on page 3 §10.
findings.fix: Move the key-change trigger bullet to page 3 §12 ("Remount On Purpose"), or gloss it in place: "a key change (see §10) — React discards the old fiber and mounts a new one."

findings.summary: The children escape hatch is presented as a memo-free trick without linking it to the automatic bailout taught on page 3, so §13 and the page-3 callout read as contradicting each other.
findings.evidence: Page 3 callout: "If props are referentially equal and no state or context changed, React clones the child fibers and skips the subtree entirely." Page 4 §13: "It breaks the parent-renders-child-renders chain." Page 4 §16: "<Wrapper><Expensive /></Wrapper> // children built by the OUTER parent // Wrapper re-renders, Expensive does not" — the mechanism is the page-3 bailout, but that is never said.
findings.fix: In §16 add "this is the page-3 bailout firing — same element object, so props are referentially equal," and in §13 note that the automatic bailout needs the identical element while memo only needs shallow-equal props.

findings.summary: The section titled "Two Distinct Jobs" is followed by a table listing three jobs.
findings.evidence: "heading","text":"19. Two Distinct Jobs" over rows ["skip slow compute"], ["keep object identity"], ["feed a dep array"]
findings.fix: Either retitle to "Three Distinct Jobs", or fold "feed a dep array" into the "keep object identity" row since it is the same referential-stability job.

findings.summary: The section headed "Two Distinct Jobs" lists three jobs, leaving the learner unsure which two were meant.
findings.evidence: Heading: "19. Two Distinct Jobs"; table rows: ["skip slow compute","CPU time saved"], ["keep object identity","downstream memo hits"], ["feed a dep array","effect stops re-firing"].
findings.fix: Either retitle to "Two Jobs, Three Payoffs" and mark rows 2–3 as the same job (referential identity), or merge them into one row: "keep object identity → downstream memo hits, deps stop re-firing."

findings.summary: useSyncExternalStore is prescribed as the fix for context's missing selector two pages before the handbook explains what it is.
findings.evidence: Page 7 §28 table: ["one field only","useSyncExternalStore"], following "Context has no selector — it is all or nothing." Its only explanation arrives on page 9 §35: ["useSyncExternalStore","selector: only affected render"] (it is also listed as a trigger on page 1 with no gloss).
findings.fix: Add the selector clause at the page 7 table or as a following bullet — "useSyncExternalStore takes a selector, so only components reading the changed field render" — instead of holding it until the page 9 tool table.

findings.summary: The identity recap inverts the precedence of key and position: React matches keyed children by key first, with position only the fallback when no key is given.
findings.evidence: "Reconciliation matches by (type, position), then key." — contradicting page 3's "Matching happens by identity, not by index."
findings.fix: Reword to "Reconciliation matches by key when present, else by position — then requires the type to match to reuse the fiber."

findings.summary: In section 44 the decision-flow chain wraps mid-row, leaving a connector arrow dangling at the right margin pointing at nothing while the final node drops to its own line.
findings.evidence: Row 1 reads "Is it actually slow? → Move state down → Pass children → memo + stable props →" with the trailing arrow at the right content edge; "Virtualize" sits alone on the line below with no incoming arrow.
findings.fix: Render flow arrows as inter-node separators that are suppressed at a line break (or wrap the chain so "→ Virtualize" moves to the next line together), matching the un-trailed chains on pages 1 and 9.
